tests.success: Recorded initial and evolved CDM velocities satisfy the canonical NFW relation to rtol=5e-15 and are transported unchanged into all four catalogue velocity columns.
tests.why: Retain this physical unit identity; it can detect unit mistakes even when tuple and catalogue code share the same error.
tests.limits: This controlled calculation does not calibrate a subhalo population against simulations or observations.
tests.failure: Any stated comparison/identity mismatch, missing expected exception/warning, or unexpected calculation error fails the case.

tests.name: test_total_matches_independent_angular_integration
tests.purpose: Integrate the differential scattering law to the total cross section.
tests.success: For velocity/scale ratios 0..100, angular quadrature meets its error target and agrees with sigma_total to rtol=5e-12.
tests.why: Retain an independent physical definition distinct from the effective transport cross section.
tests.limits: This controlled calculation does not calibrate a subhalo population against simulations or observations.
tests.failure: Any stated comparison/identity mismatch, missing expected exception/warning, or unexpected calculation error fails the case.

tests.name: test_zero_and_array_velocity_limits
tests.purpose: Recover analytic total-scattering limits for vectorized velocity inputs.
tests.success: The output keeps shape, equals sigma0 at zero velocity and sigma0/2 at v=w, and follows the high-velocity inverse-square limit to 2e-10.
tests.why: Retain these physical limits and vectorization because the total and effective cross sections have different meanings.
tests.limits: This controlled calculation does not calibrate a subhalo population against simulations or observations.
tests.failure: Any stated comparison/identity mismatch, missing expected exception/warning, or unexpected calculation error fails the case.
